basis: Inherited epidermal fragility with palmoplantar blistering in 18/18 patients.
Vertebral and epiphyseal growth abnormalities define this skeletal dysplasia umbrella; extraskeletal disease is subtype-dependent.
Immune-mediated inflammatory peripheral neuropathy; muscle weakness and atrophy reflect denervation. Respiratory involvement is occasional.
Defined by skeletal dysplasia, including pseudoachondroplasia and multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
Skin blistering, pigmentation and nail abnormalities define disease; oral blisters and dental abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Hair, retinal/cataract and dental abnormalities define syndrome; brachydactyly occurs in 80-99%. Intellectual deficit lacks sufficient frequency evidence.
Confluent and reticulated papillomatosis is a keratinization disorder producing hyperkeratotic skin lesions.
Preaxial digit duplication is a skeletal malformation; diabetic embryopathy reflects maternal diabetes, not established endocrine disease in the affected child.
Defined by impaired atrioventricular electrical conduction.
Multiple osteochondromas affect bone in 17/17 patients. Nerve compression and myelopathy lack evidence of involvement in at least 30%.
Factor IX gain of function causes inherited hypercoagulability. Venous thrombosis is a separately diagnosed consequence rather than universal vessel damage.
Fibroblastic/histiocytic mesenchymal soft-tissue tumor; anatomical site is unspecified. Histiocytic morphology alone does not establish blood or immune disease.
Inherited podocyte disease causes focal segmental glomerular scarring; immune mediation is not intrinsic to this group.
Recurrent oral ulcers define disease; skin lesions and uveitis each occur in roughly half or more. Vascular, joint and reported CNS involvement omitted under the four-axis cap.
Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor with perineurial differentiation.
Peripheral axonal damage defines disease; immune causation is uncertain across Ig classes. Associated gammopathy is separate; muscle wasting reflects denervation.
Myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm of blood and marrow, principally involving neutrophils.
Serine biosynthesis disorder with major brain malformations and ichthyosis; muscle hypoplasia, atrophy and contractures occur in 30-79%. Other malformations omitted under cap.
Benign smooth muscle tumor arising in the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
Premature fusion of cranial sutures defines disease; neurologic or visual damage is not established in most isolated cases.
Benign glioneuronal tumor arising within the central nervous system.
Defined as peripheral nerve damage caused by infection.
Choroidal atrophy within the inherited chorioretinal dystrophy spectrum.
Calpain-related skeletal muscle dystrophy with myofiber degeneration and fatty replacement; weakness does not establish peripheral nerve disease.
Absence of urine output defines urinary system dysfunction; no additional organ damage is intrinsic to this concept.
